bull.b: Subscription-based identity services create recurring revenue and provide opportunities to expand accounts as customers add users, applications, and security modules. This model can support durable retention, predictable cash generation, and deeper integration into enterprise technology environments over the next several quarters.

Very strong operating and free cash flow demonstrates effective conversion of the business model into internally generated funding. This provides flexibility to invest in products, pursue strategic opportunities, support operations, and return capital without relying heavily on external financing.

Growth among large enterprise accounts and meaningful bookings from new products indicate both strong customer relevance and expansion potential. Larger contracts and cross-sell activity can deepen platform adoption, improve account durability, and broaden Okta’s competitive position.

bear.b: Slower revenue growth reduces confidence that recent profitability gains will continue at the same pace. If expansion and new-customer momentum remain moderated, operating leverage may become harder to sustain and the company could face greater pressure to control spending.

Early customer wins establish strategic traction, but immaterial AI revenue means the opportunity has not yet become a meaningful financial contributor. Okta must convert initial deployments into repeatable, scalable revenue before AI products can materially strengthen growth or diversification.

The partner-led delivery shift may improve ecosystem leverage over time, but it reduces reported revenue in the near term because more services are performed by GSIs. That creates a measurable headwind to growth and makes underlying subscription momentum harder to assess.
